brief: Managed money delivered its biggest weekly copper sale since April 2023 between September 8 and 15, selling $2.6bn of high-grade copper futures with $2.2bn of that being liquidation, pushing fund selling to a roughly 3.5-year extreme. The December contract fell 5.6% from record highs on tariff uncertainty, doubts about the pace of the AI buildout, and broader financial conditions, with the selling landing right as copper hit its long-term trend line and 100-day moving average. The note frames this as liquidation rather than a broken structural trend: copper longs stay closely correlated with Goldman's Data Center equity basket, which fell 6.9% in the latest AI unwind, so the copper selloff reads as an AI-positioning event tied to that equity unwind rather than a break in the structural data-center demand story. It flags the White House's undecided refined-copper tariff and slower-AI-pace calls as open questions for data-center-driven copper demand, and concludes that as long as the AI trade stays alive, don't get too bearish on copper.
